IBM.rationale: IBM shows solid fundamental health with Q1 2026 revenue of $15.92B (+9.5% YoY) and EPS of $1.28 (+14.3% YoY), driven by double-digit growth in Software (+11%) and Infrastructure (+15%). Operating cash flow improved to $5.17B. The company beat consensus estimates ($1.91 EPS vs $1.81 expected) and reaffirmed 2026 guidance for 5%+ constant-currency revenue growth and ~$1B higher FCF. However, QoQ metrics show significant sequential decline (revenue -6.2%, EPS -44.6%) reflecting normal Q1 seasonality after Q4's strong software renewal cycle. Valuation has compressed dramatically: P/E of 20.5x is at the bottom of its 365-day range (20-51x), and P/B of 6.66x is also near the low end (6.5-10.8x), suggesting the market has priced in considerable pessimism. The stock is down ~20% over the past quarter. Key risks include consulting revenue pressure (signings down 15.6%), federal contract cancellations ($100M), and competitive threats from hyperscalers. The $11.6B Confluent acquisition adds data streaming capabilities but increases leverage. Near-term catalysts include the upcoming Think 2026 conference (May 18-19) and continued AI monetization through watsonx platform. The FedRAMP authorization for 11 AI products via AWS partnership could expand federal market access. Dividend yield of ~2.9% with 30 consecutive years of increases provides income support.
